subject: Sternwood: request for limited on-prem audit access + pricing ask
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <e.torres@sternwood.com>
Cc: procure@sternwood.com
Date: 2026-08-27T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood private pilot — clarifying audit window request

Hi Elena — great to speak this morning. As discussed, attaching the draft private-deployment redlines and our SOC2 report for your procurement team. Quick clarifications: Sternwood asked for quarterly 72-hour on-site forensic access to verify host-level controls and an HSM integration with customer keys.

We can support HSM-backed keys and scoped forensic exports, but host-level access and open-ended 72-hour windows are a hard constraint for us due to multi-tenant infra and third-party hardware. Our standard compromise for Private/VPC is a timeboxed snapshot (read-only logs + ephemeral forensic export) over a 12-hour window, executed under an approved legal process and monitored by Redwood security. We can commit to quarterly windows and provide an engineer as point of contact.

On pricing: Sternwood is considering a 24-month reserved plan. I'm prepared to propose a one-time onboarding credit and an 18% committed-term discount subject to executive approval and accepting the 12-hour forensic snapshot approach.

Can you confirm procure@sternwood whether the 12-hour, read-only forensic approach is acceptable so we can move to contract? If not, please outline what you must have so I can escalate.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0123

Attachments: redwood_private_hosting_draft_redlines.docx; SOC2_report_latest.pdf

From: Elena Torres <e.torres@sternwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@sternwood.com, Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@sternwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-27T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood private pilot — clarifying audit window request

Ben — thanks for the quick follow. Procurement confirms Sternwood's baseline ask: quarterly 72-hour forensic windows with host-level checks, and the HSM must allow our KMS to wrap keys (customer-controlled). The 72-hour requirement is non-negotiable for our compliance team (State Health Data regs).

We appreciate the 12-hour snapshot alternative but that will not satisfy our internal auditors unless there is supplementary proof of host immutability and a repeatable attestation. Is there a path to combining the snapshot with a signed attestation + KMS wrap demonstration? Also, your pricing note is helpful — procurement is expecting a commercial concession for the extended controls and a 24-month commitment.

Elena
Head of Procurement, Sternwood Health
Elena.Torres@sternwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-27T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Sternwood — they will push for 72h host access; need exec signoff on terms + discount

Folks — forwarding Sternwood's reply. TL;DR: they require quarterly 72-hour host-level forensic windows and customer-wrap KMS/HSM. They are willing to do a 24-month commit and expect a commercial concession because of the additional controls.

Our position: we can enable customer-controlled HSM/KMS wrapping (with network-isolated key wrap path) and provide a monitored, limited forensic export, but cannot grant host-level login or open 72-hour windows. Proposed exception: accept 12-hour read-only forensic snapshots + signed continuity attestation from Redwood security + a quarterly live KMS wrap demo. In exchange, I propose we offer an 18% committed-term discount and a one-time onboarding credit of $35k (offsets our R&D/ops work).

As this is non-standard, I need an executive approval path (Marissa: deal desk signoff on discount + legal OK; Lauren: legal comfort on attestation language and the HSM wording). Attached are their questionnaire and our redlines.

Ben

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-28T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Exec review requested — Sternwood exceptional audit/KMS terms + discount

Lauren / Marissa — bringing this across for a quick exec decision. Summary and recommended resolution below.

Summary: Sternwood Health (deal SW-2026-041) wants quarterly 72-hour host-level forensic windows + customer-wrap KMS. They are prepared to sign a 24-month reserved capacity deal with an expectation of a commercial concession.

Recommendation (one-liner): Approve a bounded exception: customer-controlled KMS wrap + HSM integration proof + quarterly 12-hour read-only forensic snapshot + Redwood-signed attestation and live KMS-demo; in return, grant an 18% committed-term discount and a $35k onboarding credit. Conditions: legal to add specific attestation language in Section 9 of the SOW, security-run playbook attached to the contract, and limit any forensic exports to aggregated/log-only artifacts (no host shell access).

Rationale: The ask materially increases operational and compliance burden but Sternwood is a large customer (projected ARR $3.2M over 24 months) and will commit to reserved capacity. The proposed concession maintains our security posture while offering Sternwood the audit surrogates their auditors need.

Questions for you:
- Marissa: approve the 18% discount and $35k onboarding credit as within our delegated discount bands? (If not, suggest an alternate % or credit)
- Lauren: can legal draft the attestation wording and confirm HSM/KMS wrap language that preserves our liability cap?

Timing: Sternwood expects a firm answer by COB Monday (2026-08-30). Ben is prepared to start redlining DocuSign after we confirm.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Head of Enterprise Sales — Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
+1 650 555 0890

Attachments: Sternwood_Security_Questionnaire_v3.pdf; redwood_private_hosting_draft_redlines.docx

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-28T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exec review requested — Sternwood exceptional audit/KMS terms + discount

Approve with conditions. Legal will accept the 12-hour read-only forensic snapshot + Redwood attestation + quarterly KMS demo as an accommodation, provided the attestation includes: a clear list of artifacts returned, a limitation that no host-level credentials will be issued, indemnity limited to proven Redwood negligence, and a requirement that Sternwood provide a mutually-agreed incident plan before any snapshot.

Marissa — commercial: 18% discount + $35k onboarding credit is acceptable within my view for a 24-month reserved commitment at projected ARR of $3.2M. Please confirm accounting treatment (deferred revenue / contract credits) but you have my signoff to proceed to DocuSign once legal adds the attestation and the security playbook is appended.

I'll have legal draft the attestation and redline Section 9 by tomorrow morning and put the redlined SOW into DocuSign.

Lauren Bishop
VP, Legal — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Subject: Sternwood — proposed path forward and commercial offer

Elena / Carlos — thanks for your patience. Per our internal review, Redwood can offer the following:

- HSM/KMS integration with customer-wrap demonstrated in a live test before go-live.
- Quarterly 12-hour read-only forensic snapshot executed under an agreed incident plan (Redwood security present), plus a signed Redwood attestation detailing returned artifacts.
- Commercial: 24-month reserved capacity, 18% committed-term discount, and a $35,000 onboarding credit.

Next steps: if you accept these terms, I'll circulate the redlined SOW with Section 9 (attestation) added and the DocuSign envelope. Please confirm by end of day Monday, 2026-08-30, so we can lock capacity for the quarter.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
